_meta.preparation_standard: Targeted gems from Isa 58 — the fast Jehovah chooses (v6), the dawn light (v8), the 'Here I am!' answer (v9). Each verse gets 2-6 word color-coded underlines; v6 and v9 get four-slot voice notes.

notes.content: Notice how Jehovah redefines fasting in this verse. Most of us hear the word 'fast' and think — give something up. Skip a meal. Deny yourself. Verse 6 says no — the fast Jehovah picks is loosening the shackles, sending oppressed ones away free, breaking the yoke. It's not about what you take FROM yourself. It's about what you take OFF somebody else. That flips the whole frame. Religious self-denial, in Jehovah's eyes, isn't really religious unless it ends up making someone else's life lighter. The truest 'fast' has nothing to do with the meal you skipped. It has to do with the chain you helped break.

underlines.phrase: your light will shine through like the dawn
the glory of Jehovah will be your rear guard

notes.content: Look at the very last words of Isaiah 58:9 — 'Here I am!' We usually picture us calling out to Jehovah, like a kid calling for a parent. But notice — this verse flips it. We call out, then Jehovah responds — 'Here I am!' That's the same phrase Samuel used when Jehovah called him as a boy in 1 Samuel 3. Same posture, same readiness — but here, the parent is the one saying it to the kid. Jehovah is the one ready to be called on. Not waiting to be impressed. Not waiting to be earned. Just ready. 'Here I am.' That's how he answers.
